target: DuplexCascade as German Frankenstein 2.0 full-duplex candidate versus architecture donor
generation_reason: A newly identified 2026 VAD-free cascaded full-duplex system is materially different from the generation-1 speech-native candidate set and generation-2 AEC prerequisite: it may transfer turn-control architecture while independently failing German production-language support.
source_summary: The official DuplexCascade paper/repository implement a local modular streaming ASR-LLM-TTS full-duplex pipeline driven by fixed micro-turns and explicit conversational control tokens. The official Hugging Face model declares English, and the released demo invokes an English/French STT config; no pinned primary source establishes German speech or German E2E performance.
transfer_hypothesis: Map the source-supported micro-turn control semantics onto Frankenstein's existing VoiceIntent/GWT arbitration using accepted German ASR/TTS components rather than adopting the released English Qwen2-7B stack as the production voice.
remaining_falsifiers: A newer official German DuplexCascade checkpoint/config may change language eligibility.
German streaming ASR partial instability may make fixed micro-turn arbitration worse than the current endpoint path.
A smaller local dialogue model may not retain adequate semantic turn-control accuracy.
Periodic controller inference may create enough compute contention to worsen end-to-end latency.
VAD safety-signal retention and learned turn-control arbitration require an explicit non-conflicting policy.
next_discriminator: After the existing self-hosted runner gate is restored and queued ASR runtime work is consumed, run a distinct bounded Frankenstein-native micro-turn-controller benchmark on clay-direct-dev: German ASR partials -> fixed 0.6 s micro-turns -> explicit WAIT/RESPOND/INTERRUPT/BACKCHANNEL candidate -> current VoiceIntent/GWT arbitration, with VAD retained as an observed safety signal. Measure premature takeover, stop latency, backchannel precision, partial-correction sensitivity, TTFT and resource contention.
